Priority name: Student Pathways, Access, and Outcomes
Title: Early learning pathways
Exact agenda question: What do longitudinal literacy and mathematics pathways reveal about when differences in achievement, placement, and risk first emerge?
Draft synthesis: NC Pre-K studies use both participant and county-funding designs. The added middle-school follow-up reports sustained favorable funding associations; kindergarten findings remain more conditional. Shared cohorts and funding data limit independence across papers.

Priority name: Student Pathways, Access, and Outcomes
Title: Middle-grades transitions
Exact agenda question: What prior academic, attendance, intervention, placement, and school-context factors predict Grade 8 mathematics placement and success?
Draft synthesis: Wake County’s targeted middle-school acceleration study offers evidence about students near a test-score cutoff. It does not answer every question about grade 8 placement statewide.

Priority name: Student Pathways, Access, and Outcomes
Title: Advanced learning access
Exact agenda question: Who participates in advanced learning opportunities, including AIG, honors, AP/IB, advanced mathematics, CCP, advanced CTE, CDM, and related pathways, and where are the largest opportunity gaps?
Draft synthesis: CCP research adds delivery and participation evidence: advising, remaining costs, schedules, and transportation shape opportunities. These qualitative findings complement, rather than establish, effects of changing access rules.

Priority name: Student Pathways, Access, and Outcomes
Title: Postsecondary pathways
Exact agenda question: How do students transition from high school into postsecondary education, credentials, and other outcomes, and which K–12 experiences are associated with successful transitions?
Draft synthesis: Early-college lottery evidence supports credential attainment. CCP analyses add favorable education and recorded-earnings associations, with selection and employment-data limits. They do not establish that one pathway or delivery format is best.

Priority name: Student Pathways, Access, and Outcomes
Title: School-sector pathways
Exact agenda question: How do enrollment, mobility, access, and outcomes vary across school contexts, including charter schools and for populations such as Students with Disabilities?
Draft synthesis: Charter research adds behavioral and civic outcomes for historical ninth-grade entrants. The early Opportunity Scholarship study reports positive estimates with strong volunteer-sample and test-comparability limits. Neither establishes current sector-wide superiority.

Priority name: Workforce Capacity, Working Conditions, and Professional Support
Title: Supply and stability
Exact agenda question: Where are vacancies, attrition, mobility, and staffing shortages concentrated across educators, school leaders, and specialized instructional support personnel, and which working conditions best predict subsequent workforce instability across educator experience levels and school contexts?
Draft synthesis: The agency summary provides recent attrition measures; rural interviews add local perspectives on why retention can be difficult. Together they identify issues for follow-up rather than proving a retention strategy works.

Priority name: Workforce Capacity, Working Conditions, and Professional Support
Title: Working conditions
Exact agenda question: How do school leadership, planning time and workload, educator voice, safety, professional learning, and instructional support relate to staff well-being, retention, and effectiveness; are there recurring combinations of conditions or thresholds associated with elevated risk?
Draft synthesis: Earlier NC research links workplace conditions to observed retention. The 2026 TWC report adds descriptive evidence about intended career plans; rural interviews provide context. These different measures should be interpreted separately.

Priority name: Workforce Capacity, Working Conditions, and Professional Support
Title: Qualifications and staffing
Exact agenda question: How are licensure, certification, staffing ratios, caseloads, and other workforce characteristics associated with student and organizational outcomes?
Draft synthesis: Teacher-assistant and ATR studies address different staffing arrangements. The ATR class-size report proposes team ratios that include release time, but its small one-year analysis cannot establish class-size effects.

Priority name: Workforce Capacity, Working Conditions, and Professional Support
Title: Professional learning and leadership
Exact agenda question: Which professional learning, coaching, leadership, and role-design approaches improve educator practice and support, and how do leadership, time, safety, and professional learning interact to influence workforce outcomes?
Draft synthesis: ATR and coaching sources examine different forms of support. New LETRS observations describe instructional strengths and remaining problems after training, without estimating training effects. ALTER still needs pilot validation; CARES findings remain preliminary.

Priority name: Workforce Capacity, Working Conditions, and Professional Support
Title: Bright spots
Exact agenda question: Which schools and districts achieve stronger workforce stability or teacher working conditions than expected given their context, or show sustained improvement across survey administrations, and what organizational practices distinguish them?

Priority name: Effectiveness, Implementation, and Return on Investment
Title: Effectiveness
Exact agenda question: What effects are associated with major state, local, and federally funded (e.g., Title I-IX) initiatives, policies, programs, and activities, including their effects on educator working conditions, retention, and student outcomes?
Draft synthesis: The collection now includes early Read to Achieve and Opportunity Scholarship evaluations, early-childhood funding research, and ATR and Restart studies. Their populations, policy periods, and designs differ; agency summaries are not independent impact replications.

Priority name: Effectiveness, Implementation, and Return on Investment
Title: Implementation
Exact agenda question: How do implementation, dosage, fidelity, staffing, leadership, educator workload, and local context influence effectiveness?
Draft synthesis: LETRS observations, CCP interviews, and preliminary coaching reports describe how support and access work in practice. Such evidence helps define improvement questions but does not establish that a proposed change causes better outcomes. ATR annual case studies add district-specific evidence about roles and coaching time.

Priority name: Effectiveness, Implementation, and Return on Investment
Title: Variation in effects
Exact agenda question: Which students, schools, districts, or communities benefit most or least, and why?
Draft synthesis: The indexed early-learning and mathematics studies illustrate variation by context, outcome, or student group. Subgroup findings require careful attention to the underlying design.

Priority name: Effectiveness, Implementation, and Return on Investment
Title: Cost and return on investment
Exact agenda question: What are the costs associated with different approaches relative to their outcomes, and when do benefits justify costs?
Draft synthesis: Teacher-assistant research offers historical staffing evidence. The tutoring project is investigating delivery models, but a complete cost comparison was not reviewed here.

Priority name: Effectiveness, Implementation, and Return on Investment
Title: Scalability and transferability
Exact agenda question: Which promising approaches can be implemented successfully across different North Carolina contexts?

Priority name: Effectiveness, Implementation, and Return on Investment
Title: New initiatives and pilots
Exact agenda question: How effectively are newly funded programs, staffing or organizational redesigns, and instructional innovations implemented, and which improve working conditions, educator stability, or student outcomes?
Draft synthesis: The Pender County project update documents design and preparation. No retention impact findings were reviewed.

Priority name: Effectiveness, Implementation, and Return on Investment
Title: Emerging instructional approaches and technologies
Exact agenda question: How do new instructional models, educational technologies, and AI-enabled tools affect teaching practices, student learning, educator workload, and operational efficiency?

Priority name: Effectiveness, Implementation, and Return on Investment
Title: Continuation and expansion decisions
Exact agenda question: Which investments demonstrate sufficient effectiveness, feasibility, and cost-effectiveness to warrant continuation, modification, expansion, or discontinuation?

Priority name: Effectiveness, Implementation, and Return on Investment
Title: Title I/II/III/IV investments
Exact agenda question: Explore which federal spending patterns and funded activities are associated with stronger student outcomes, including achievement gap reduction, and under what conditions.

Priority name: Effectiveness, Implementation, and Return on Investment
Title: Early Literacy Specialists
Exact agenda question: Identify credible measures and feasible evaluation approaches to understand how Early Literacy Specialists contribute to student learning, teacher practice, and school capacity.

Priority name: Effectiveness, Implementation, and Return on Investment
Title: FINCH kindergarten readiness implementation
Exact agenda question: Examine FINCH’s usability and feasibility for Read to Achieve purposes, and how its use could affect kindergarten assessment decisions and growth measurement.

Priority name: Effectiveness, Implementation, and Return on Investment
Title: National Board certification and bonus programs
Exact agenda question: Investigate the longer-term effects of National Board certification and bonus programs, including the linked workforce and funding data needed for credible evaluation.

Priority name: Effectiveness, Implementation, and Return on Investment
Title: Cell phone policies
Exact agenda question: Explore outcomes associated with changes in school and district cell phone policies, where available data and evaluation conditions support meaningful comparisons.

Priority name: Effectiveness, Implementation, and Return on Investment
Title: Mathematics interventions and Foundations courses
Exact agenda question: Examine how mathematics interventions and Foundations courses support student learning and readiness for subsequent coursework, and how results vary across students and implementation approaches.

Priority name: Effectiveness, Implementation, and Return on Investment
Title: Scheduling and delivery models
Exact agenda question: Explore how school schedules and instructional delivery models relate to learning opportunities, student outcomes, and staffing needs, and which approaches work best in different settings.
Draft synthesis: The NC dual-enrollment modality abstract reports favorable postsecondary outcomes across formats versus nonparticipation, while pass rates differ. It is not a randomized comparison of online and in-person provision.

Priority name: Effectiveness, Implementation, and Return on Investment
Title: Family engagement strategies
Exact agenda question: Examine how family engagement strategies support participation in schooling, attendance, and student learning, including which approaches reach families facing barriers to engagement.
Draft synthesis: The community-school pilot describes family engagement during local implementation. It offers ideas to examine rather than a comparative effectiveness ranking.

Priority name: Effectiveness, Implementation, and Return on Investment
Title: School safety practices
Exact agenda question: Explore how school safety practices are implemented and how they relate to student and staff perceptions of safety, school climate, and learning conditions.
Draft synthesis: Discipline reform and digital monitoring address different risks. The indexed evidence distinguishes observed disciplinary outcomes from perceived technology effectiveness.

Priority name: Effectiveness, Implementation, and Return on Investment
Title: School health and behavioral health initiatives
Exact agenda question: Examine how school health and behavioral health initiatives affect access to services, student well-being, attendance, and learning, including differences across schools and student groups.
Draft synthesis: A rural telemedicine study offers evidence about school-based healthcare access. It does not establish the effectiveness of all behavioral-health initiatives.

Priority name: Effectiveness, Implementation, and Return on Investment
Title: School-based Medicaid expansion
Exact agenda question: Explore how expanded school-based Medicaid services affect access to student supports, district service capacity, and financing, including the costs and challenges of implementation.

Priority name: Effectiveness, Implementation, and Return on Investment
Title: Disaster-recovery supports
Exact agenda question: Examine how disaster-recovery supports help schools restore services and support student attendance, well-being, and learning, and how needs and recovery vary across communities.

Priority name: Effectiveness, Implementation, and Return on Investment
Title: Charter transportation and nutrition models
Exact agenda question: Compare charter school transportation and nutrition service models, their costs, and promising approaches to meeting student needs, including lessons from other states.

Priority name: Effectiveness, Implementation, and Return on Investment
Title: Educator preparation and workforce pipeline initiatives, including teacher apprenticeships and principal development supports
Exact agenda question: Examine how educator preparation, teacher apprenticeships, and principal development supports contribute to workforce entry, readiness, and retention, and how outcomes vary across programs and settings.

Priority name: Effectiveness, Implementation, and Return on Investment
Title: Extended learning, integrated student supports, and attendance early-intervention programs
Exact agenda question: Explore how extended learning, integrated student supports, and early attendance interventions relate to student engagement, attendance, and academic progress, including implementation conditions and costs.
Draft synthesis: The Union County summary reports favorable early outcomes. Its public project page does not provide the full analysis needed for a confident transfer or scaling decision.

Priority name: Effectiveness, Implementation, and Return on Investment
Title: AI-supported instruction, digital learning platforms, and curriculum modernization
Exact agenda question: Examine how AI-supported instruction, digital platforms, and curriculum changes affect teaching and learning, including implementation demands, access, and differences in outcomes across students.

Priority name: Effectiveness, Implementation, and Return on Investment
Title: Career and postsecondary pathways, including CTE modernization and innovative learning models
Exact agenda question: Explore how career and postsecondary pathway models expand access to learning opportunities and support transitions beyond high school, including differences in participation and outcomes.
Draft synthesis: Early-college and CCP evidence spans credentials, employment, modality, and participation experiences. Related outputs from the same evaluation partnership should not be counted as independent replications.

Priority name: Effectiveness, Implementation, and Return on Investment
Title: School nutrition and other policies designed to reduce barriers to learning
Exact agenda question: Examine how school nutrition and other supports reduce barriers to participation and learning, including their reach, implementation costs, and relationships with attendance and student outcomes.

Priority name: Attendance, Safety, Health, and School Climate
Title: Attendance
Exact agenda question: What student, family, school, health, and community factors are most strongly associated with chronic absenteeism and attendance recovery?
Draft synthesis: NC studies document persistent absence, learning associations, and particular healthcare or policy pathways. A historical charter-entry study adds favorable attendance estimates for that choice context; it does not establish a universal attendance intervention.

Priority name: Attendance, Safety, Health, and School Climate
Title: Safety and discipline
Exact agenda question: How do school safety conditions, student conduct, educator perceptions of safety, and disciplinary practices relate to staff well-being and stability, student behavior, and academic outcomes?
Draft synthesis: Early-grade reform and disparity studies address exclusion and fairness. A separate historical charter-entry study adds behavioral outcomes, but does not identify which discipline practices explain its estimates.

Priority name: Attendance, Safety, Health, and School Climate
Title: Health and student supports
Exact agenda question: How do access to counselors, social workers, psychologists, nurses, behavioral health services, and community supports relate to attendance, discipline, crisis events, and academic outcomes?
Draft synthesis: The indexed rural telemedicine study connects healthcare access to attendance. It leaves broader questions about counselors, psychologists, nurses, and social workers unresolved.

Priority name: Attendance, Safety, Health, and School Climate
Title: School climate
Exact agenda question: How are staff and student perceptions of leadership, safety, belonging, support, and climate associated with teacher retention, student attendance, academic growth, and differences in outcomes across student groups?
Draft synthesis: Working-conditions research, the 2026 TWC report, and a community-school pilot provide complementary perspectives. Staff perceptions and intentions should be distinguished from measured workforce and student outcomes.

Priority name: Attendance, Safety, Health, and School Climate
Title: Family engagement
Exact agenda question: Which family engagement approaches are most effective in North Carolina contexts, including rural communities and engagement of fathers and other caregivers?
Draft synthesis: The rural community-school pilot offers an implementation example. Comparative evidence across family-engagement approaches has not yet been assembled here.

Priority name: Attendance, Safety, Health, and School Climate
Title: Resilience and recovery
Exact agenda question: Which school, district, workforce, and community conditions support stronger recovery following major disruptions?
Draft synthesis: Attendance and engagement studies document persistent barriers; tutoring and preliminary CARES findings add specific intervention examples. Agency-reported coaching findings do not establish the overall effects of pandemic relief.

Priority name: Assessment, Accountability, and Decision Support
Title: Assessment selection and use
Exact agenda question: What are the relative strengths, limitations, feasibility, and instructional implications of different assessment and screening approaches?
Draft synthesis: The Opportunity Scholarship assessment review is complemented by a historical achievement study whose estimates depend partly on the test family used by participating schools. That study does not identify one universally best assessment.

Priority name: Assessment, Accountability, and Decision Support
Title: Longitudinal interpretation
Exact agenda question: How can assessment information be used to identify meaningful learning trajectories, emerging risk, and changes in student performance over time?

Priority name: Assessment, Accountability, and Decision Support
Title: Interim assessment
Exact agenda question: Where can NC Check-Ins and other interim measures support valid targeting, cohort monitoring, and instructional decisions, and where should interpretation be limited?

Priority name: Assessment, Accountability, and Decision Support
Title: Instructional use
Exact agenda question: How are schools and districts translating screening, benchmark, EOG, EOC, and other assessment information into instructional and intervention decisions, and which routines support effective use?

Priority name: Assessment, Accountability, and Decision Support
Title: Accountability reporting
Exact agenda question: How should assessment, accountability, and school climate or workforce indicators, including Teacher Working Conditions (TWC) results, be reported so meaningful differences, trends, and school profiles remain visible and useful?
Draft synthesis: The assessment review addresses cross-sector comparisons. The 2026 TWC report provides a workforce-reporting example, documenting response denominators and aggregation. These sources address distinct reporting needs.

Priority name: Assessment, Accountability, and Decision Support
Title: Accountability validity
Exact agenda question: How well do specific accountability measures, school benchmarks, and workforce survey constructs or composite indices predict subsequent outcomes, remain stable over time, and perform across school and district contexts?

Priority name: Policy Design, Resource Allocation, and Governance
Title: Resource allocation and school finance
Exact agenda question: How do alternative funding formulas, allotment structures, and resource allocation policies affect the distribution, adequacy, flexibility, and use of educational resources across schools and districts?
Draft synthesis: The initial sources cover historical finance analysis, teacher-assistant staffing, and planned ESSER priorities. These measures do not provide a current causal comparison of funding formulas.

Priority name: Policy Design, Resource Allocation, and Governance
Title: Student access and opportunity
Exact agenda question: How do enrollment, assignment, eligibility, and participation policies influence access to educational opportunities, and what are their consequences for student pathways and outcomes?
Draft synthesis: Mathematics, school-choice, and CCP work address different entry processes. New CCP interviews describe practical access barriers; the historical voucher analysis has a selective sample and does not establish outcomes under current eligibility rules.

Priority name: Policy Design, Resource Allocation, and Governance
Title: Workforce and organizational flexibility
Exact agenda question: How do policies governing educator qualifications, staffing, planning time, leadership roles, educator voice, and operational authority influence working conditions, recruitment, retention, instructional capacity, and school effectiveness?
Draft synthesis: ATR and Restart studies address specific models. The separate ATR staffing report explains team ratios and data needs; it does not establish that larger classes are harmless or that a ratio rule improves outcomes.

Priority name: Policy Design, Resource Allocation, and Governance
Title: Policy implementation and administrative burden
Exact agenda question: How do state and local requirements, educator workload, administrative structures, and operational constraints influence policy feasibility, consistency, costs, and effectiveness?
Draft synthesis: The ATR class-size report identifies the need to link teacher leaders, supported teachers, students, and release time for team-level reporting. It offers a feasibility approach, not a tested estimate of reduced burden.

Priority name: Policy Design, Resource Allocation, and Governance
Title: Distributional effects and policy tradeoffs
Exact agenda question: How would proposed policy changes affect different students, schools, districts, and communities, and what tradeoffs arise among competing policy objectives?
Draft synthesis: The indexed finance review and immigration-enforcement study examine distinct distributional issues. They inform selected dimensions rather than a comprehensive ranking of policies.

Priority name: Policy Design, Resource Allocation, and Governance
Title: Policy monitoring and evaluation
Exact agenda question: How can longitudinal data, comparative analyses, and appropriate evaluation designs inform decisions about maintaining, modifying, expanding, or discontinuing policies?
Draft synthesis: Agency workforce reporting and ESSER-plan analysis illustrate useful descriptive monitoring. Descriptive trends and plans alone cannot determine whether a policy caused improvement.

Priority name: Policy Design, Resource Allocation, and Governance
Title: Weighted-student funding and alternative state school finance models
Exact agenda question: Compare how weighted-student funding and alternative school finance models distribute resources across districts and student needs, including implications for equity, adequacy, and local planning.
Draft synthesis: The indexed 2019 finance study offers a framework for considering adequacy and alignment. It does not simulate a current weighted-student formula.

Priority name: Policy Design, Resource Allocation, and Governance
Title: Low-wealth supplemental funding and resource distribution
Exact agenda question: Examine how low-wealth supplemental funding reaches districts and students with greater resource needs, and how allocation patterns relate to educational opportunities and local capacity.

Priority name: Policy Design, Resource Allocation, and Governance
Title: School assignment, open enrollment, and educational choice policies
Exact agenda question: Explore how assignment, open enrollment, and school choice policies shape access, enrollment patterns, and student outcomes, including implications for transportation and district planning.

Priority name: Policy Design, Resource Allocation, and Governance
Title: Automatic enrollment in advanced coursework
Exact agenda question: Examine how automatic enrollment policies affect access to advanced coursework, participation, and subsequent performance, including whether opportunity gaps narrow across schools and student groups.
Draft synthesis: Wake County’s earlier threshold-based approach offers a related NC example. It should not be described as an evaluation of the later statewide policy.

Priority name: Policy Design, Resource Allocation, and Governance
Title: Educator licensure and alternative staffing arrangements
Exact agenda question: Explore how licensure requirements and alternative staffing arrangements affect workforce supply, qualifications, stability, and student outcomes, including differences across school contexts.

Priority name: Policy Design, Resource Allocation, and Governance
Title: Innovative school models and operational flexibility
Exact agenda question: Examine how innovative school models use operational flexibility and how those choices relate to educational opportunities, organizational capacity, and student outcomes.
Draft synthesis: Its outcome pattern varies across subjects and measures. The model should be studied as implemented, rather than equated with every innovative-school approach.

Priority name: Policy Design, Resource Allocation, and Governance
Title: School nutrition and student access policies
Exact agenda question: Explore how school nutrition eligibility, access, and service policies affect participation and barriers to learning, including differences across schools, communities, and student groups.

Priority name: Policy Design, Resource Allocation, and Governance
Title: Statewide policy implementation and administrative requirements
Exact agenda question: Examine how statewide policy requirements are interpreted and implemented locally, including administrative burden, consistency across districts, and opportunities to simplify processes while preserving accountability.
